home.IND@HOU: Houston’s 44-22 road demolition of the Chargers shows the scoring ceiling to exploit Indianapolis’ defense, which allows 27.1 points per game.
home.ARI@KC: Kansas City has scored 35 in consecutive wins, while Arizona managed nine total points across its last two games.
home.BAL@CAR: Carolina owns wins over Detroit and Philadelphia, while Baltimore has lost five straight and Lamar Jackson is on Injured Reserve.
home.MIA@BUF: Buffalo’s three straight wins came by 26, 17 and 19 points, while Miami ranks 29th with a -5.1 rating.
home.NO@CHI: Chicago is 7-2 with a +3.9 rating, while New Orleans has three offensive linemen listed Out or Doubtful.
home.PIT@PHI: The model keeps Philadelphia within 3.9 points, making the Eagles’ 4.5-point home cushion sufficient against a Pittsburgh team coming off a 38-18 loss.
home.TB@DET: Detroit has won five straight and averages 28.6 points, while Tampa Bay enters with Baker Mayfield Questionable.
home.TEN@DAL: Dallas averages 28.6 points and carries a +3.4 offensive rating against Tennessee, the sheet’s 32nd-ranked team with a -6.8 rating.
home.NYJ@LAC: The Chargers just won at Baltimore, while New York has lost five straight and been outscored 66-24 over its last two games.
home.JAX@NYG: New York is 5-3-1 and has beaten Dallas and Philadelphia, making six home points substantial protection despite Jacksonville’s strong form.
home.LV@DEN: Denver’s +3.9 rating dwarfs Las Vegas’ -3.7, and the Broncos have won five straight while the Raiders have lost five of six.
home.MIN@SF: San Francisco averages 31.2 points and has scored 84 across consecutive wins, enough offensive force to clear three at the neutral site.
home.CIN@WSH: The model makes Cincinnati only a five-point winner, leaving Washington a 1.5-point cushion against the 6.5-point market spread.

away.IND@HOU: Indianapolis already beat Houston 19-17, and the model projects only a 6.2-point Texans win, leaving ample room inside 12.5.
away.ARI@KC: Arizona owns three road wins, and the model limits Kansas City to a 10.4-point victory, well below 15.5.
away.BAL@CAR: Baltimore has already won at Indianapolis and Atlanta, while the model has Carolina winning by only 1.8 against a 2.5-point spread.
away.MIA@BUF: Miami stayed within two points at Indianapolis last week, and the model projects a 13.3-point margin rather than Buffalo’s 16.5-point spread.
away.NO@CHI: New Orleans has road wins at Baltimore and New York, while the model’s 8.9-point margin stays comfortably inside Chicago’s 11.5-point spread.
away.PIT@PHI: Philadelphia has lost seven straight and scores 16.4 points per game, while 6-3 Pittsburgh held New Orleans and Cleveland to 10 and 6.
away.TB@DET: Tampa Bay allows only 19.8 points per game, while Detroit is missing Aidan Hutchinson and Kerby Joseph; the model keeps the margin at 5.1.
away.TEN@DAL: Dallas allows 28.2 points per game and surrendered 46 last week, while the model projects a seven-point game, inside 8.5.
away.NYJ@LAC: Los Angeles is 1-8 and scores only 16 points per game; the model projects a three-point Chargers win, putting New York inside 3.5.
away.JAX@NYG: Jacksonville enters on a 42-7, 33-10 and 40-23 run, and the model projects a 6.5-point win against a six-point line.
away.LV@DEN: Three of Denver’s last four wins came by five points or fewer, and the model puts Las Vegas within 9.1 against a 10-point spread.
away.MIN@SF: At a neutral site, Minnesota allows just 14 points per game, and the model projects only a one-point San Francisco win against a three-point spread.
away.CIN@WSH: Cincinnati has won five straight, every victory by at least seven points, while Washington enters just 3-5-1.
